articles.title: Constl Achieves 1.6 Tbps Transmission on Live NLD Network With Ciena Across Mumbai ...
articles.content: Technology For SMEs News Constl Achieves 1.6 Tbps Transmission on Live NLD Network With Ciena Across Mumbai–Pune Corridor The achievement makes Constl the first in India to successfully complete a 1.6 Tbps channel over an NLD network, according to Ciena, and marks a further step in Constl’s effort to scale high-capacity optical connectivity across its network. SMEStreet Edit Desk 03 Oct 2026 15:42 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 Constl, a pan-India carrier-neutral connectivity provider and subsidiary of Space World Group, has successfully completed a 1.6 Tbps channel transmission over its live national long-distance (NLD) network across the Mumbai-Pune corridor, using Ciena’s WaveLogic 6 Extreme (WL6e) technology. The achievement makes Constl the first in India to successfully complete a 1.6 Tbps channel over an NLD network, according to Ciena, and marks a further step in Constl’s effort to scale high-capacity optical connectivity across its network. The milestone follows Constl and Ciena’s 1 Tbps transmission achievement in 2025, representing a 60% increase in demonstrated channel capacity. The latest transmission was completed on a live production network, rather than a laboratory or test environment. This demonstrates Constl’s ability to deploy next-generation optical capacity under operational network conditions and strengthens its network scalability for bandwidth-intensive services. “Achieving 1.6 Tbps on a live production network across Mumbai – Pune corridor marks another important step in Constl’s network evolution, enabling us to support 800GE services and growing AI bandwidth demands with greater efficiency and a lower cost per bit,” said Ankit Goel, Chairman and Founder, Space World Group and Founder, Constl. “With our growing pan-India fibre network, these advances in optical capacity enable us to scale our network and support the increasingly demanding requirements of hyperscalers, data centres and AI-driven applications.” From 1 Tbps to 1.6 Tbps: scaling optical capacity The latest achievement builds on Constl and Ciena’s earlier 1 Tbps transmission across a 1,450-km Mumbai-Chennai long-haul route in 2025, which was completed without regeneration. That milestone demonstrated Constl’s ability to deploy high-capacity optical transmission over long-haul distances. The progression to 1.6 Tbps on a live NLD network further expands the capacity available per optical channel and supports Constl’s roadmap for terabit-scale connectivity across key network corridors. Ciena’s WL6e technology supports up to 1.6 Tbps coherent capacity and is designed to extend 800G connectivity across long-distance network links, while improving spectral efficiency and reducing cost and power requirements per bit. For Constl, the higher-capacity optical channel provides additional headroom to address growing requirements from hyperscalers, data centres, cloud platforms and AI-driven applications, where increasing volumes of data need to move between compute, storage and network infrastructure. Supporting India's growing digital infrastructure requirements India’s expanding data-centre, cloud and AI ecosystem is increasing demand for high-capacity connectivity between major digital infrastructure hubs. Constl is leveraging WL6e to scale multi-terabit capacity across its NLD and metro routes, connecting key cities and data-centre locations. articles.title: Vande Bharat crosses Chenab, Anji bridges at 100 kmph - Kashmir Vision
articles.content: Katra-Banihal train speed limit raised, say officials Jammu: A Vande Bharat Express crossed the world’s highest railway bridge over the Chenab River and India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge at Anji at 100 kmph, as the maximum permissible speed on the 111-km-long Katra-Banihal broad-gauge rail section was raised to 100 kmph, officials said. The speed enhancement on the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section under the Jammu division of Northern Railway was successfully tested on Thursday, marking a significant operational milestone for the ambitious Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Railway Link (USBRL) project. “The maximum permissible speed on the 111-km-long Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section has been increased from 75 kmph to 100 kmph,” Senior Divisional Commercial Manager Uchit Singhal said. He said the Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26401/26404) created a new record by crossing both the world’s highest Chenab Bridge and India’s first cable-stayed Anji Bridge at 100 kmph. The 111-km Katra-Banihal section is a crucial and technically challenging component of the USBRL project, which is aimed at providing seamless rail connectivity between the Kashmir Valley and the rest of the country. The Railway Ministry approved the enhancement in the maximum permissible speed to 100 kmph after all prescribed safety conditions were complied with by the Railways in August this year, officials said. Earlier, trains were permitted to operate at a maximum speed of 85 kmph on the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Sangaldan section and 75 kmph on the Sangaldan-Banihal section. The increase in the permissible speed is expected to make train operations on the USBRL project smoother, reduce travel time and provide faster, safer and more comfortable journeys to passengers. With the enhancement, travel time between Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra and Banihal is also expected to come down, providing faster and more comfortable rail connectivity in the region. The Katra-Banihal section traverses some of the most difficult and rugged terrain of the Pir Panjal and lower Himalayan ranges, involving deep valleys, steep mountain slopes, major rivers and highly complex geological formations. The construction of the line has therefore required extensive use of advanced engineering techniques, including long tunnels, high-level bridges and sophisticated railway infrastructure, officials said. The section has some of the country’s most prestigious and challenging engineering structures, including the Chenab Railway Bridge, the world’s highest railway bridge, constructed over the Chenab River near Reasi, and the Anji Khad Railway Bridge, India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge. The section also has 33 tunnels. Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the Katra-Srinagar Vande Bharat Express from Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra on June 6, 2025. articles.title: Kumkum Mohod wins India's first women's individual recurve gold at Asian Games
articles.content: ANI Photo | Kumkum Mohod wins India’s first women’s individual recurve gold at Asian Games Indian archer Kumkum Mohod secured a historic victory at the Asian Games 2026 on October 3, becoming the first Indian woman to win gold in the individual women’s recurve event. The 17-year-old triumphed over South Korea’s Oh Yejin in a closely contested shoot-off, prevailing 6-5 after the match was tied 5-5 following five sets. The final was decided by a single arrow, with Oh scoring an 8 before Mohod maintained her composure to land a perfect 10 and clinch the title, as reported by ESPN. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google The match began with Oh taking the opening set 29-27, establishing a 2-0 lead. The second set ended tied at 29-29, giving Oh a 3-1 advantage. Mohod responded with three consecutive 10s in the third set for a perfect 30, while Oh scored 29, levelling the match at 3-3. Oh then edged ahead by winning the fourth set 28-27. Facing elimination in the fifth set, Mohod again shot three 10s to score 30 while Oh managed 28, forcing the shoot-off. Mohod’s decisive arrow to the 10-ring secured the gold medal. ADVERTISEMENT Mohod’s gold capped an impressive campaign that included winning women’s recurve team gold and mixed team silver on the previous day. She teamed with Ankita Bhakat and Kirti Sharma to defeat South Korea 5-3 in the women’s recurve team final, marking India’s first-ever Asian Games medal in this event. Later, she partnered with Dhiraj Bommadevara to win silver in the mixed recurve team event after a 3-5 loss to China. During her individual event run, Mohod defeated South Korean world and Olympic champion Kang Chaeyoung 6-4 in the quarterfinals and China’s world championship silver medallist Zhu Jingyi 6-2 in the semifinals. This gold medal adds to India’s previous individual recurve medal, a silver by Tarundeep Rai at the 2010 Guangzhou Games, while marking the country’s first women’s individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. ADVERTISEMENT With Mohod’s individual gold, India’s medal tally at the Games has reached 77, comprising 17 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals at the time of reporting. articles.title: TAPAS-1 Satellite : India's Private Thermal Imaging Mission - INSIGHTS IAS
articles.content: Source: IE Subject: Science and Technology Context: Ahmedabad-based spacetech startup Satleo Labs launched TAPAS-1 , India’s first commercial private thermal-imaging payload, aboard SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket via the Transporter-18 rideshare mission from California. TAPAS-1 About TAPAS-1 : What it is? The Thermal Access Platform for Analytics & Solutions (TAPAS-1) is India’s first indigenously designed commercial private thermal-imaging nanosatellite payload, built as a 1.5-kg modular CubeSat. It acts as an orbital thermometer for the Earth, capturing variations in thermal infrared radiation emitted from the planet’s surface. Developed by: Satleo Labs , an Ahmedabad-based spacetech startup incorporated in 2023 by entrepreneur Shravan Singh Bhati, retired ISRO scientist Dr. Ranendu Ghosh, and business strategist Urmil Bakhai. Launch Vehicle : SpaceX Falcon 9 (part of the 130-satellite Transporter-18 dedicated rideshare mission). Orbital Profile: Deployed into a 500-km Sun-Synchronous Low Earth Orbit (LEO) . Mission Lifespan: Designed for a 3-year baseline operational mission, to be followed by TAPAS-2 and the planned PYRO constellation (10–15 microsatellites) by 2029. Aim: To provide sovereign, cost-effective, high-resolution thermal intelligence directly to commercial, civic, and defense users, democratizing access to Earth observation analytics without requiring dedicated ground station hardware. Key Applications & Features: Urban Heat Island (UHI) Mapping: Tracks micro-level surface temperature gradients across dense city sectors, equipping urban municipal bodies with precise thermal data to mitigate heat stress and guide climate-resilient zoning. Precision Agriculture & Water Stress Management: Measures soil surface moisture depletion and crop evapotranspiration, allowing farmers and agrarian enterprises to detect crop stress and optimize micro-irrigation scheduling before visible foliage damage occurs. Wildfire & Thermal Disaster Tracking: Detects subterranean smoldering, tracks active forest fire fronts through smoke haze, and identifies industrial hot spots in near real-time. Subsurface Geological & Archaeological Detection : Leverages differences in thermal inertia to spot hidden subterranean ruins, buried geological faults, and potential shallow mineral/hydrocarbon deposits. Direct-to-User AI Integration: Combines onboard thermal sensors with cloud-based machine learning to convert raw measurements into sector-specific predictive insights.

articles.title: Jawahar Dweep Becomes India's First Plastic-Free Oil Terminal - GKToday
articles.content: Home Jawahar Dweep Becomes India’s First Plastic-Free Oil Terminal Jawahar Dweep Becomes India’s First Plastic-Free Oil Terminal October 3, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal in Mumbai was declared plastic-free on 2 October 2026 by the Mumbai Port Authority. The terminal became India’s first oil terminal to eliminate single-use plastics completely. Jawahar Dweep and Mumbai Port Jawahar Dweep is also known as Butcher Island and is an offshore facility located about four kilometres off Mumbai’s coast. It has five jetties and handles crude oil and petroleum products. The terminal serves major refineries such as Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited, Indian Oil Corporation Limited, and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation. Petroleum cargo accounts for nearly three-fifths of Mumbai Port’s total traffic. Plastic-Free Port Operations The plastic-free declaration was made during Swachhata Abhiyan 2026 at Grey Gate in Indira Dock. The programme was held on 2 October, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi . The Mumbai Port Authority has planned reductions in single-use plastics across its docks, residential colonies, and coastal areas. The initiative covers operational and residential spaces under the port administration. Oil Spill Response Facilities Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal dedicated the port’s new Oil Spill Response facilities to the nation on 2 October 2026. Oil Spill Response systems are used for containment, recovery, and control of marine oil pollution. Important Facts for Exams Jawahar Dweep is an offshore oil terminal located in Mumbai Harbour. Butcher Island is another name for Jawahar Dweep. Single-use plastics are items designed for one-time use before disposal. 2 October is observed as Gandhi Jayanti in India. articles.title: Mumbai Port's Jawahar Dweep Becomes India's First Plastic-Free Oil Terminal - Swarajya
articles.content: Oct 03, 2026 | Updated 08:56 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . The Mumbai Port Authority declared its Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal plastic-free yesterday (2 October), marking a significant environmental milestone for India's maritime sector. The offshore facility becomes the country's first oil terminal to completely eliminate single-use plastics, with the announcement made during the Swachhata Abhiyan 2026 cleanliness programme held to mark Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary. The island terminal, also known as Butcher Island, consists of five berths handling crude oil and petroleum products approximately four kilometres off Mumbai's coast. The facility serves major refineries including BPCL, HPCL, IOCL, and ONGC, and petroleum cargo accounts for nearly three-fifths of Mumbai Port's overall traffic. Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal addressed the achievement at the programme, stating that a plastic-free Jawahar Dweep demonstrates India's ports can maintain growth whilst preserving environmental standards. He also dedicated new Oil Spill Response facilities to the nation during the event. The Mumbai Port Authority banned single-use plastics across its premises from September 2021, following the Prime Minister's national call to curb plastic pollution. The port authority has now committed to extending similar measures across its docks, residential colonies, and coastal areas throughout the remainder of the year. Earlier, trains were permitted to operate at a maximum speed of 85 kmph on the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Sangaldan section and 75 kmph on the Sangaldan-Banihal section. The Katra-Banihal section traverses some of the most difficult and rugged terrain of the Pir Panjal and lower Himalayan ranges, involving deep valleys, steep mountain slopes, major rivers and highly complex geological formations. The section has some of the country’s most prestigious and challenging engineering structures, including the Chenab Railway Bridge, the world’s highest railway bridge, constructed over the Chenab River near Reasi, and the Anji Khad Railway Bridge, India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge. articles.title: Vande Bharat Hits 100 kmph on Kashmir Rail Link Across Key Bridges - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Vande Bharat Hits 100 kmph on Kashmir Rail Link Across Key Bridges Breaking News Vande Bharat Hits 100 kmph on Kashmir Rail Link Across Key Bridges By Urban Acres October 3, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Indian Railways has raised the maximum permissible speed on the 111-km Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section of the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link from 75 kmph to 100 kmph, after Vande Bharat Express trains successfully completed trials across the Chenab and Anji bridges at the higher speed. The trial was conducted with Vande Bharat Express trains 26401 and 26404. During the run, the trains crossed the Chenab Rail Bridge, described as the world’s highest railway arch bridge, and the Anji Bridge, India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge, at 100 kmph. The speed enhancement follows the Railways’ clearance of the section after it met the required safety parameters. Earlier, the maximum permissible speed was 85 kmph between Katra and Sangaldan and 75 kmph between Sangaldan and Banihal. The revised limit standardises the maximum permissible speed for the 111-km Katra-Banihal section at 100 kmph, according to the report. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw shared a video of the trial on X and called the development a historic milestone. The successful run demonstrates the operational use of two of the USBRL project’s most technically significant structures while the railway link continues to connect the Jammu region with the Kashmir Valley. The Chenab Rail Bridge stands 359 metres above the riverbed and spans 1,315 metres. The Anji Bridge rises 331 metres above the riverbed and stretches 725 metres across the valley. Their inclusion in the trial run places the bridges at the centre of the latest operational milestone, rather than treating them only as construction achievements. The Katra-Banihal section is a crucial part of the rail connection between the Jammu region and the Kashmir Valley. The increase in permissible speed is expected to improve operational efficiency, reduce travel time and provide a faster and more comfortable journey for passengers using the route. The development also marks a shift from construction and engineering milestones towards the performance of the completed railway infrastructure in regular operations. The higher speed limit will apply after the Railways’ safety clearance for the section. The latest trial involved the Vande Bharat trains crossing both landmark bridges at 100 kmph, with the revised operating parameters now forming the next stage of the USBRL corridor’s development.
